items.claim: The negative-particle chain the row uses as its cohesion glue is misattributed on one verse and stops one token short of the rear seam, where the same particle plus two further byte-true links cross into the verse the row calls a register pivot.
items.evidence: Word-bound sweep splitting the patach-pointed negative from the segol-pointed preposition, run over the span and its rear neighbour: oshb:Eccl.5.1 = web:Eccl.5.2 carries two BARE negatives (אַל תְּבַהֵ֨ל and אַל יְמַהֵ֛ר, byte tier) and NO waw-prefixed form -- the waw in that verse sits on וְלִבְּךָ֧ (byte tier), not on the particle. The waw-prefixed form the row attributes to oshb:Eccl.5.1 is at oshb:Eccl.5.5 = web:Eccl.5.6 (וְאַל תֹּאמַר֙, byte tier, beside bare אַל תִּתֵּ֤ן). The row's arithmetic (5 tokens / 3 verses) is byte-correct; the locative attribution is not. SEAM: the same particle continues at oshb:Eccl.5.7 = web:Eccl.5.8 (אַל תִּתְמַ֖הּ, byte tier) -- one verse past this row's own rear seam -- so oshb:Eccl.5.1-Eccl.5.7 holds 6 tokens over 4 verses out of 21 negative tokens over 15 verses book-wide (sweep: 21 tokens / 15 verses, word-bound, patach-only), while the row asserts a register pivot exactly there. Two further undisclosed continuities over that same seam: חֵ֖פֶץ at oshb:Eccl.5.3 = web:Eccl.5.4 (in span) against הַחֵ֑פֶץ at oshb:Eccl.5.7 = web:Eccl.5.8 (sweep: 8 verses book-wide carry a chet-pe-tsade token); and this row's own opening imperative שְׁמֹ֣ר at oshb:Eccl.4.17 = web:Eccl.5.1 against שֹׁמֵ֔ר at oshb:Eccl.5.7 (sweep: 5 verses book-wide carry the contiguous shin-mem-resh skeleton -- oshb:Eccl.4.17, 5.7, 11.4, 12.3, 12.11 -- the first two being this row's opening verse and its rear neighbour). VERIFIED CORRECT: the seam-verse inline unpointed ketiv רגליך standing before its pointed qere רַגְלְךָ֗ at oshb:Eccl.4.17 = web:Eccl.5.1 (byte tier, matches the K/Q inventory); the patach/segol homograph discipline note, which the same verse's own אֶל בֵּ֣ית (byte tier) makes live; the fear-God close at oshb:Eccl.5.6 = web:Eccl.5.7 (byte tier); and every dual citation in the row is arithmetically right.

items.claim: The row's stated ground for isolating the verse -- that it shares no vocabulary with either neighbour -- is byte-false on three counts against its front neighbour.
items.evidence: The rejected alternative states the verse introduces a new topic 'sharing no vocabulary with either neighbor', and the rationale narrows it to vow/mouth and profit vocabulary; the unqualified form is refuted three times over on the front side. (1) הַחֵ֑פֶץ (oshb:Eccl.5.7 = web:Eccl.5.8, byte tier) against חֵ֖פֶץ (oshb:Eccl.5.3 = web:Eccl.5.4, byte tier) inside the preceding unit -- sweep: 8 verses book-wide carry a chet-pe-tsade token, two of them these. (2) שֹׁמֵ֔ר (oshb:Eccl.5.7, byte tier) against the preceding unit's OPENING imperative שְׁמֹ֣ר (oshb:Eccl.4.17 = web:Eccl.5.1, byte tier) -- sweep: 5 verses book-wide on the contiguous shin-mem-resh skeleton (oshb:Eccl.4.17, 5.7, 11.4, 12.3, 12.11); the spelling שָׁמ֥וּר at oshb:Eccl.5.12 = web:Eccl.5.13 carries the same root but escapes that contiguous sweep on its infixed waw, so the root actually runs across three rows of this cluster. (3) אַל תִּתְמַ֖הּ (oshb:Eccl.5.7, byte tier) is the sixth token of the negative-particle chain the preceding row builds its cohesion case on (sweep: 21 negative tokens over 15 verses book-wide, word-bound and patach-only; oshb:Eccl.5.1-Eccl.5.7 holds 6 over 4 verses). ENGAGEMENT: the device note discloses that same clause in English only ('don't marvel'), with no pointed form quoted for it, so the one boundary-relevant Hebrew observation the row makes about its own deviation ships without its quoted run. VERIFIED CORRECT: all three quoted runs reach byte tier at oshb:Eccl.5.7; the crosswalk web:Eccl.5.8 = oshb:Eccl.5.7 is right; the district term is a genuine LBH/Persian-loan site; oshb:Eccl.5.7 carries NO K/Q note (the inventory's nearest offset-zone notes are oshb:Eccl.5.8 and oshb:Eccl.5.10), so no disclosure is owed and none is claimed.

items.claim: Every Hebrew claim in the row is byte-true -- the ketiv/qere sits exactly where the row places it, on the third-person pronoun -- and the lexical-isolation ground survives a token check against both neighbours.
items.evidence: The full-verse quote reaches byte tier at oshb:Eccl.5.8 = web:Eccl.5.9, and the inline unpointed ketiv היא does stand immediately before its pointed qere ה֑וּא, i.e. on the third-person pronoun as stated -- the inventory confirms oshb:Eccl.5.8 = web:Eccl.5.9 as one of the four offset-zone K/Q sites. Token check I ran against both neighbours at skeleton tier: oshb:Eccl.5.7 (web:Eccl.5.8) and oshb:Eccl.5.9 (web:Eccl.5.10) share NO content token with oshb:Eccl.5.8, so the isolation ground holds on the bytes rather than on theme. The crux disclosure is argued from the pointed bytes (לְשָׂדֶ֖ה נֶעֱבָֽד, byte tier) rather than from the WEB rendering, and the row declines to adjudicate while holding confidence at low -- the correct posture for a verse the book plan registers as a difficult-syntax-plus-K/Q region. ONE LEG IS NON-DISCRIMINATING RATHER THAN WRONG, recorded so a rev round does not lean on it: 'K/Q-bearing' cannot by itself isolate this verse, since the inventory puts FOUR of the twelve book-wide notes inside this cluster's own span (oshb:Eccl.4.17 = web:Eccl.5.1, oshb:Eccl.5.8 = web:Eccl.5.9, oshb:Eccl.5.10 = web:Eccl.5.11, oshb:Eccl.5.17 = web:Eccl.5.18), and the immediately following verse bears one without being isolated on that ground. The lexical-isolation leg carries the row unaided.

items.claim: The row twice places the oshb:Eccl.5.10 ketiv/qere on a pronoun when its own byte-quoted run shows the note sitting on a construct noun, and its rear-boundary ground -- no lexical link to 'satisfied' -- is refuted on both sides of that seam.
items.evidence: The row's OWN quote, byte tier at oshb:Eccl.5.10 = web:Eccl.5.11, reads the unpointed ketiv ראית followed by the pointed qere רְא֥וּת -- a construct noun ('the seeing of'), governing עֵינָֽיו; the only pronominal element in the clause is the suffix on that noun, which bears no note. The row calls the note-bearing word 'the pronoun' in the rationale AND again in the device note ('the pronoun bearing the note sits outside this word'), so the error is doubled, and it is contradicted by the bytes the row itself spliced. The pronoun description belongs to the PREVIOUS verse's note (oshb:Eccl.5.8, היא / ה֑וּא), which reads as a carry-over. Skeleton sweeps keep the two objects apart: resh-aleph-waw-tav 9 verses, resh-aleph-yod-tav 19 verses. REAR-BOUNDARY GROUND REFUTED: the rationale isolates web:Eccl.5.12 as 'lacking a lexical link to loves/satisfied/advantage' and the rejected alternative repeats 'shares no vocabulary'. The satisfaction object crosses that seam: יִשְׂבַּ֣ע at oshb:Eccl.5.9 = web:Eccl.5.10 (this row, byte tier) against וְהַשָּׂבָע֙ at oshb:Eccl.5.11 = web:Eccl.5.12 (the next row, byte tier) -- the two sites the book's own three-way homograph split assigns to satisfied/satiety rather than to the swear or seven objects (sweep: 7 verses on the contiguous shin-bet-ayin skeleton across three objects; the satisfaction object holds oshb:Eccl.1.8, 4.8, 5.9, 5.11, 6.3). The eat root crosses it too: אוֹכְלֶ֑יהָ at oshb:Eccl.5.10 against יֹאכֵ֑ל at oshb:Eccl.5.11 (both byte tier); the contiguous skeleton sweep for aleph-kaf-lamed returns 11 verses and MISSES oshb:Eccl.5.10 on its infixed waw, so this link is byte-observed, not sweep-derived, and a sweep-only check would have hidden it. PLACEMENT ERROR: גַּם זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל (byte tier) is the VERSE-FINAL clause of oshb:Eccl.5.9, standing after the second (בֶּהָמ֖וֹן) clause -- not 'closing its own opening clause' as the row states. COUNT DISCIPLINE: the per-chapter hevel digit is cited without naming its numbering space, which the offset-zone counting rule requires for any chapter digit touching chs 4-5; here the digit is 2 in both spaces (oshb:Eccl.5.6 and 5.9 = web:Eccl.5.7 and 5.10) and the row's membership claim is correct, so the defect is disclosure, not arithmetic. The row also holds medium confidence over oshb:Eccl.5.9-Eccl.5.10 although the plan registers that stretch as a low-confidence syntax-and-K/Q region.

items.claim: The row's sole boundary ground -- that the verse shares no content token with either neighbour -- is byte-false in both directions, and it is asserted without naming the swept object or carrying a digit.
items.evidence: FRONT SIDE: וְהַשָּׂבָע֙ (oshb:Eccl.5.11 = web:Eccl.5.12, byte tier) against יִשְׂבַּ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.5.9 = web:Eccl.5.10, byte tier) -- the same satisfaction object under the book's byte-verified three-way homograph split (sweep: 7 verses on the contiguous shin-bet-ayin skeleton spanning satisfied / swear / seven; the satisfaction object holds oshb:Eccl.1.8, 4.8, 5.9, 5.11, 6.3, so the two adjacent sites here are two of that object's five). And יֹאכֵ֑ל (oshb:Eccl.5.11) against אוֹכְלֶ֑יהָ (oshb:Eccl.5.10 = web:Eccl.5.11, byte tier), the same eat root -- a link the contiguous aleph-kaf-lamed sweep (11 verses) misses on the infixed waw. REAR SIDE: לֶֽעָשִׁ֔יר (oshb:Eccl.5.11, byte tier) against עֹ֛שֶׁר at oshb:Eccl.5.12 = web:Eccl.5.13, the opening verse of the very case narrative the row says shares nothing with it; the sweeps separate the spellings (ayin-shin-yod-resh 3 verses: oshb:Eccl.5.11, 10.6, 10.20; ayin-shin-resh 7 verses including oshb:Eccl.5.12, 5.13, 5.18, 6.2), so this one is root-level across two lexemes -- rich man against riches -- which is exactly the move the rendering makes as well, and it is the semantic hinge from the rich man's sleeplessness to riches kept to their owner's harm. The claim is stated unqualified in the rationale and again in the rejected alternative, with no swept object named and no digit, against the campaign's count-object discipline; nothing in the row would survive a reviewer running the three sweeps above. VERIFIED CORRECT: both quoted runs reach byte tier at oshb:Eccl.5.11 = web:Eccl.5.12; the crosswalk and the single-verse span form are right; and the device note is byte-true -- neither the hevel inventory nor the under-the-sun inventory lists oshb:Eccl.5.11, so no refrain attaches to this verse.

items.evidence: VERIFIED STRONG, and stronger than the row claims: רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה at oshb:Eccl.5.12 = web:Eccl.5.13 and רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה at oshb:Eccl.5.15 = web:Eccl.5.16 are BYTE-IDENTICAL codepoint for codepoint, accents included (I compared the two runs' codepoint sequences directly), and the skeleton sweep returns exactly 2 verses book-wide -- so the row's 'exact phrase repetition' is true at byte tier and the bracket is exclusive to this span. All three quoted runs reach byte tier at their cited refs, every dual citation is arithmetically right, and the paseq handling is correct and conservative: the inventory's seg at oshb:Eccl.5.17 = web:Eccl.5.18 does fall OUTSIDE this span, and the row makes no positional claim about a count-only layer. UNDISCLOSED CROSS-SEAM DEVICE: תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.5.12 = web:Eccl.5.13, byte tier), which the row quotes inside its own opening formula, recurs at oshb:Eccl.5.17 = web:Eccl.5.18 as תַּֽחַת הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ (byte tier) immediately across this row's rear seam, carried by the same first-person report verb -- רָאִ֖יתִי at oshb:Eccl.5.12 and רָאִ֣יתִי at oshb:Eccl.5.17 (inventory: 27 under-the-sun verses book-wide, MT ch 5 holding oshb:Eccl.5.12 and oshb:Eccl.5.17; sweep: 18 verses carry the 1cs report verb, three of them the opening verses of three consecutive rows here -- oshb:Eccl.5.12, 5.17, 6.1). The pointing differs between the two sites -- הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ at oshb:Eccl.5.12 (pausal) against הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ at oshb:Eccl.5.17, both byte tier -- so the recurrence is a skeleton-tier formula match, not byte identity; but it is precisely the refrain class the campaign names as making cross-seam cohesion live, and the row discloses an adjacent paseq while passing over it. TRANSLATION-DEPENDENT SEAM ARGUMENT: the rear boundary is argued as a pivot 'introduced by “Behold” at web:Eccl.5.18' with no pointed form quoted in this row, so the load-bearing marker at that seam is a rendering rather than a byte.

items.claim: Two disclosure objects falling inside this row's own span go unstated -- one of them disclosed instead by the neighbouring row -- and the ketiv/qere gloss is attached to the wrong word of the row's own quoted run.
items.evidence: GLOSS/QUOTE PARITY: the row's byte-tier run מִסְפַּ֧ר יְמֵי חיו חַיָּ֛יו אֲשֶׁר (oshb:Eccl.5.17 = web:Eccl.5.18) puts the inline unpointed ketiv חיו before the pointed qere חַיָּ֛יו -- 'his life'. The row glosses the note as sitting on 'his days', which is the PRECEDING word יְמֵי and bears no note; the K/Q site and its crosswalk are right, the word the gloss names is not. OWN-SPAN PASEQ UNDISCLOSED, ASYMMETRICALLY: the paseq inventory places a seg at oshb:Eccl.5.17 = web:Eccl.5.18, this row's own opening verse. The row does not mention it; the PRECEDING row does, explicitly noting it as 'belonging to the following row's opening verse'. The same object is therefore disclosed on one side of a seam and not by the row that owns it, which is the symmetry failure the campaign treats as a sweep-level defect rather than a spot fix. OWN-SPAN REFRAIN UNDISCLOSED: תַּֽחַת הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ (byte tier) also falls at oshb:Eccl.5.17 (inventory: 27 under-the-sun verses; MT ch 5 holds oshb:Eccl.5.12 and 5.17), so this row's opening verse repeats both the refrain and the 1cs report frame רָאִ֣יתִי (oshb:Eccl.5.17, byte tier) of the case just closed at oshb:Eccl.5.12 = web:Eccl.5.13 and of the case opening the next row at oshb:Eccl.6.1 -- the front-seam pivot is argued from the presentative and the good/proper evaluation alone, with the continuity left unstated. REAR-SEAM ANTITHESIS UNDERSTATED (disclosed, so not charged as suppression): what crosses into oshb:Eccl.6.2 is not only the hiphil of the give-power verb but an extended construction -- ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִים֩ עֹ֨שֶׁר וּנְכָסִ֜ים and לֶאֱכֹ֤ל מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ (both byte tier at oshb:Eccl.5.18 = web:Eccl.5.19) each occur in exactly 2 verses book-wide, oshb:Eccl.5.18 and oshb:Eccl.6.2 and nowhere else, so the cohesion across that seam is materially tighter than the row's 'same verb' phrasing conveys. VERIFIED CORRECT: all three quoted runs reach byte tier at their cited refs; oshb:Eccl.5.17 = web:Eccl.5.18 is correctly identified both as a K/Q site and as one of the five eat-and-drink enjoyment sites; the duals are arithmetically right.

items.claim: Two of the row's three front-seam grounds fail on the evidence: a chapter break is tier-4 metadata that is never boundary evidence, and the claimed first-person-to-third-person shift runs the opposite way at the actual seam.
items.evidence: TIER-4 AS BOUNDARY EVIDENCE: the rationale names 'a chapter break' as one of three grounds that 'together mark web:Eccl.6.1 as its own new case', and the rejected alternative repeats 'the chapter boundary ... argue for a fresh row'. Chapter and verse numbers are tier-4 metadata and are never boundary evidence in this campaign; the ground has to be struck, not re-weighted. PERSON-SHIFT CLAIM INVERTED AT THE SEAM: the row argues 'a shift from first-person testimony to a third-person a man... scenario'. On the bytes the preceding row ENDS third-person -- גַּ֣ם כָּֽל הָאָדָ֡ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָֽתַן ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִים֩ at oshb:Eccl.5.18 = web:Eccl.5.19 and יִזְכֹּ֖ר at oshb:Eccl.5.19 = web:Eccl.5.20 (both byte tier) -- while this row's own OPENING verse is first-person: יֵ֣שׁ רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ at oshb:Eccl.6.1 carries the 1cs report verb רָאִ֖יתִי (byte tier; sweep: 18 verses book-wide carry it, including oshb:Eccl.5.12, 5.17 and 6.1). The third-person scenario begins only at אִ֣ישׁ (oshb:Eccl.6.2), inside the row. The seam therefore runs third-person into first-person, the reverse of the claim. FORMULA CLAIM UNLABELLED FOR TIER: יֵ֣שׁ רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.6.1, byte tier) is NOT byte-identical to יֵ֚שׁ רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.5.12 = web:Eccl.5.13, byte tier) -- חוֹלָ֔ה (oshb:Eccl.5.12) is absent and אֲשֶׁ֥ר (oshb:Eccl.6.1) inserted, and the accentuation differs on the first two words. The match holds at skeleton tier only (sweep: the two-word case-report opener occurs in 3 verses book-wide, oshb:Eccl.5.12, 6.1, 10.5, plus the shared report-verb-and-refrain tail); 'matching the formula' ships without the tier it is true at. DISCLOSURE OBJECTS: the paseq inventory places a seg at oshb:Eccl.6.2, INSIDE this span, and a second at oshb:Eccl.6.3 immediately across the rear seam -- neither is mentioned; and oshb:Eccl.6.2 carries the hevel refrain (זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל, byte tier, an inventory verse), while the row cites the device inventory for the under-the-sun refrain only. VERIFIED CORRECT: both quoted runs reach byte tier; oshb:Eccl.6.1 is a genuine under-the-sun site; ch-6 refs need no dual qualifier (identity outside the offset zone) and every ch-5 dual in the row is arithmetically right; and the cross-seam give-power antithesis is disclosed rather than suppressed -- indeed understated, since ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִים֩ עֹ֨שֶׁר וּנְכָסִ֜ים and לֶאֱכֹ֤ל מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ each occur in exactly 2 verses book-wide, oshb:Eccl.5.18 and oshb:Eccl.6.2.
